title: Evolution of the Human Brain
text: The human brain has undergone dramatic evolutionary changes over the past 7 million years since our lineage diverged from that of chimpanzees. Early hominids like Australopithecus had brain sizes of about 400–500 cc, similar to modern chimpanzees. Homo habilis (2.4–1.4 million years ago) showed the first significant increase, to about 600 cc, associated with tool use. Homo erectus reached 900–1100 cc. Homo sapiens has a brain averaging about 1,350 cc. The expansion of the prefrontal cortex is associated with higher cognitive functions including abstract reasoning, language, and planning. Genetic changes in genes like FOXP2 contributed to human language capacity.
